description: What the Copilot should do with a question: which sources the planner must select, which it must not, and whether the maintenance documentation covers it. Two readers: the offline planner test in apps/api/tests, which needs no network, and `ml copilot evaluate`, which scores a running stack. `corpus_covers` is about the documentation only -- a refusal is expected when a question asks the corpus and the corpus cannot answer, which is why the two facts are separate.

questions.question: Why is M003 becoming risky and what should I inspect according to the SOP?
questions.note: PRD.md AC-007, verbatim. It asks two things at once -- why risk is rising, and what to do about it -- so every source is in scope: 'risk' selects the telemetry, trend and prediction tools, and 'inspect'/'SOP' select the corpus.

questions.question: What happened to M003 during the last five hours?
questions.note: MASTERPLAN.md section 6's own negative example, and the one that matters most: a question about what a machine has been doing must not read the manuals. The window also selects incidents, because a five-hour window is a period something might have happened in.

questions.question: What is the current temperature of M003?
questions.note: A named signal selects the series and its trend. No risk word appears, so the prediction tool is not required -- and asserting it as *forbidden* would over-constrain a question the model's output is legitimately adjacent to. Named M005 until the first live run: only M003 is registered on the deployment, so the Copilot refused with `unknown_machine` before it reached any telemetry tool, and the scorecard called that a tool selection failure. A question about an unregistered machine is a real case, but it is a different one.

questions.question: What should I inspect on M003 according to the maintenance manual?
questions.note: 'Inspect' and 'manual' are documentation words; the machine is named, so the current state comes along as context. Nothing asks about risk, so nothing asks the model.

questions.question: How many incidents has M003 had?
questions.note: An incident question reads the incident record and nothing else.

questions.question: What is the torque spec for the M003 gearbox output shaft?
questions.note: The demonstration's negative control: the corpus has no torque specification, so the answer must be a refusal. Identical in form to the evaluation set's own unanswerable questions, which is why the threshold was calibrated on those.

questions.question: Which grease is approved for electric motor bearings?
questions.note: No machine is named, so no machine tool may be selected -- there is nothing for one to read. The corpus is the only source that can answer, and this one it can.

questions.question: Is M003 at risk of failing?
questions.note: The mirror of the negative example: a risk question stays out of the manuals. 'Risk' and 'failing' select the trend and the model; nothing asks what to do about it.

questions.question: What calibration interval does ISO 17025 require for the plant flow meters?
questions.note: From the retrieval set's unanswerable five, whose scores calibrated the sufficiency threshold. A single refusal case is not a rate, which is why two of them are here.

questions.question: What is the rated current specification for the M003 motor?
questions.note: Names a machine, so the planner also reads the current state -- and still must refuse, because the question is about a figure no finding contains. Replaced 'how many litres of coolant does the chiller hold' after the evaluation set found that the planner has no word for a specification question: that one tripped nothing, so no corpus lookup happened and the refusal never had a chance. 'Rated' and 'spec' are now triggers; the class is wider than the words, which the changelog says out loud.
